r2SourceEvidence.review_note: This settlement in southeastern Iran was not a Sumerian polity. The prior 5000–1000 BCE numbers reflect the date span attached to a Pleiades representative location, not a verified continuous occupation. Wikipedia gives c. 3550–2300 BCE while UNESCO gives c. 3200–1800 BCE. The revised game interval is the broad outer envelope of those estimates; the game cannot express endpoint uncertainty or gaps. End is exclusive; -1799 includes the approximate 1800 BCE endpoint. Blank civHint means no asserted civilization ID, not that the site was uninhabited.

before.note: Norte Chico; not Inca. civHint is a placeholder until a pack id exists.

after.note: Caral-Supe/Norte Chico, not Inca. No civilization id is asserted; dates are a gameplay approximation.

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Caral is a Late Archaic Andean site and not Inca; the old Inca id was marked as a placeholder. No replacement civilization id is inferred. The existing 2600–2000 BCE reference interval is retained; sources disagree on earlier and later limits, so it should not be treated as precisely dated. The related 3000 BCE Supe Valley event is regional and does not assert a city at that date.

Neolithic Knossos is on Crete, not Sumer. A blank civilization hint preserves the uncertainty; no Bronze Age or palace-era polity is assigned to the Neolithic site. Existing approximate span and coordinates are unchanged; this span ends before the game’s -3000 time floor. A separate Minoan-tagged Knossos site overlaps and needs its own chronology review.
